obligations.definition: The interface includes an independent UART, PS/2 keyboard reception, and ASCII conversion of the keyboard queue head. The two receivers share clk/rst_n; the keyboard queue head connects to the conversion input, while the UART transmit input remains externally driven, with no implicit automatic forwarding between them.
obligations.setup: Establish known legal inputs and the necessary reset/history according to the interface contract; internal signals must not be forced.
obligations.stimulus: Drive the UART RX/TX and PS/2 inputs separately; run them independently and concurrently, confirming that the keyboard head feeds only ASCII and is not automatically forwarded to the UART. Reset and check the public outputs of the three functional roots.
obligations.expected: The interface includes an independent UART, PS/2 keyboard reception, and ASCII conversion of the keyboard queue head. The two receivers share clk/rst_n; the keyboard queue head connects to the conversion input, while the UART transmit input remains externally driven, with no implicit automatic forwarding between them.
obligations.sampling: The clk period is 20ns; drive on falling edges and accept on the next rising edge; observe at 2ns and 8ns after the edge. The 16 acceptance edges after the last raw keyboard stop-bit falling edge constitute the filtering/write transition, after which every frame must be checked; an empty head has no data obligation, and a nonempty head must be checked.
obligations.checker: Build UART transaction counts, PS/2 filtering and frame history, three capacity-4 queues, and character mapping based only on reset, inputs, and their history; do not read DUT actual to generate expected. obligations.definition: The keyboard queue has depth 4 and width 9; the two UART queues have depth 4 and width 8. A nonempty head is a combinational output. A read alone advances when nonempty, and a write alone advances when not full; simultaneous read and write advance only when neither empty nor full, with no empty bypass or full replacement. Reset clears only logical occupancy and does not erase storage.

An empty head has no obligation; a nonempty head must be compared.

obligations.definition:
rd_data[8:0] is the complete lookup key, and ascii[7:0] is the combinational result for the current key. There is no clock, reset, handshake, state, or fixed cycle latency; observe after the input is stable and combinational propagation has occurred. Consecutive inputs are independent of previous keys.



The low 8-bit scan codes 1c 32 21 23 24 2b 34 33 43 3b 42 4b 3a 31 44 4d 15 2d 1b 2c 3c 2a 1d 22 35 1a represent a through z, respectively, in that order; bit8=0 outputs ASCII 61 through 7a, and bit8=1 outputs 41 through 5a. All values are hexadecimal.



When bit8=0, scan codes 45 16 1e 26 25 2e 36 3d 3e 46 output 30 through 39 in order; scan codes 0e 4e 55 54 5b 5d 4c 52 41 49 4a 29 5a 66 output 60 2d 3d 5b 5d 5c 3b 27 2c 2e 2f 20 0d 08 in order. bit8=1 defines no alternate characters for these special characters; the unmatched rule applies. All values are hexadecimal.



Any input that does not exactly match one of the complete 9-bit keys above outputs 2a, including keys containing X or Z; it neither retains the previous output nor outputs zero as the default.
obligations.setup: Establish known legal inputs and the necessary reset/history according to the interface contract; internal signals must not be forced.
obligations.stimulus: Through PS/2, construct unshifted and shifted letters, digits, symbols, special keys, and unmatched 9bit keys in sequence; independently compare ASCII using the specified mapping when the queue head is valid. Use consecutive different keys to check the absence of history; exhaustive testing of 512 keys in the independent character-conversion subtask serves as additional evidence. Check the X/Z default only when the independent conversion input can be driven directly; do not claim it is reachable from two-state PS/2.
